name: Off-Highway Vehicle
description: A self-propelled vehicle designed primarily for use off the public highways and commonly used for recreation, including dirt bikes; an electric dirt bike built for off-road riding is one, whatever its power or speed. It is registered with Colorado Parks and Wildlife rather than the DMV and kept off public roads except routes opened to it. Defined by Colorado Revised Statutes §33-14.5-101(3).
restrictions: Designed to travel on wheels or tracks, primarily for use off the public highways
No limit on motor power or speed
Residents must register it with Colorado Parks and Wildlife each year (April 1 to March 31) and display the decals to ride it, or even have it at a staging area
A nonresident-owned or -operated one needs a Colorado OHV permit, unless it carries a valid home-state registration and has been in Colorado no more than 30 consecutive days
May be titled for off-highway use at a county motor vehicle office

Not allowed on public streets, roads or highways except to cross them, at permitted events, in emergencies, or where the state opens a road or a local ordinance designates an OHV route, which can't include a state highway
On federal public land, ridden only on routes signed or otherwise authorized for motorized travel
On a road or route opened to it, no one under 10 may ride it, and an unlicensed rider must stay within sight of a supervisor holding a valid driver's license
On a street or road, local governments may require eye protection, a helmet for riders under 18, and no more than two riders on a motorcycle
On public land it needs working brakes, and a lit headlamp and taillamp between sunset and sunrise
